### What is broken

The automatic check scans the code for rule violations, then scans the same source files again before writing its summary. The repeat adds four minutes to every run.

### Why it is broken

The step that writes the check's summary runs its own scan instead of reusing the first scan's results. Both scans take four minutes and list the same files. We tried giving the summary step the first scan's file list. The extra four minutes disappeared, and the summary stayed exactly the same.

### How to fix it

Change the one place in the code that starts the second scan so it reuses the file list that already exists. This saves four minutes per run and leaves the summary unchanged. Choose hotfix because the fix changes only one place in the code and the tried change already showed the result.

### What is broken

The report says the chart disappears after refresh. With your sample data of ten rows, the chart stayed visible after refresh in both Chrome and Firefox. Both browsers used settings with no saved preferences.

### Why it is broken

We could not make the chart disappear. Clearing the browser's stored copy of the data did not change that, so the cause is still unknown.

### What happens next

Could you tell us how many rows the failing dataset has? We need that number to continue.

### What is broken

Nothing is broken. Opening `/widgets/` shows page not found (404) as intended, and `/widgets` opens the page.

### Why it is broken

The part that matches web addresses to pages accepts only exact addresses. The documented rules for page addresses say a final slash is not accepted ([widget addresses](https://example.org/docs/widget-addresses)).

### What happens next

The correct address is `/widgets`, without the final slash. No fix or ticket is needed.

### What is broken

Opening `/widgets/` shows page not found (404), while `/widgets` opens the page. Nothing is broken under the documented address rule.

### Why it is broken

The part that matches web addresses to pages compares them exactly. It accepts `/widgets` but rejects `/widgets/`, as the documented rule requires.

Use `/widgets` without the final slash. No fix or ticket is needed: the documentation explicitly states that trailing slashes are not accepted ([address rules](https://example.org/docs/widget-addresses)).
